anomalies.observed: U3 is populated as an ATtiny13V-10S and its VCC pin (8) is tied to the +5V rail (the LM1117 output net labelled +5V, also seen on U3's pin 8 in the right-hand tile).
anomalies.expected: The 'V' grade ATtiny13V is specified for a 1.8 V–3.6 V supply only; at a +5 V rail the correct part would be the ATtiny13-10S (1.8–5.5 V). The companion THT option U2 (ATtiny45-20P) is rated for 5 V, so the rail is intended to be 5 V.

evidence.quote: U3 ATtiny13V-10S ... pin 8 VCC on +5V (right side of sheet 1, second tile)
U1 LM1117 ... VO -> +5V; U2 ATtiny45-20P pin 8 -> +5V

anomalies.impact: If the SMD footprint U3 is populated, its VCC exceeds the ATtiny13V absolute operating maximum (3.6 V); the chip is over-volted and may fail or behave unreliably, unlike the 5 V-tolerant ATtiny45 option.

anomalies.observed: The LM1117 output (+5V net) is decoupled only by C2 = 100 nF; no bulk output capacitor is present anywhere on the +5V rail.
anomalies.expected: Standard practice (LM1117 datasheet) requires a >=10 uF output capacitor for loop stability; 100 nF alone leaves the linear regulator prone to oscillation.

evidence.quote: C2 100nF between +5V and GND; U1 LM1117 VO -> +5V

anomalies.impact: The 5 V rail can oscillate under load, destabilising the MCU supply.
